original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 30 Out-of-Band Remote Access structure, manufacturer identity and supported inbound/outbound connection modes against the approved platform specification without altering or exercising management control.
original_method: Collect complete raw Type 30 through protected read-only OS access, bind it to the SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/parser identity, decode all connection-mode flags and manufacturer strings, compare to the expected matrix and optionally correlate only redacted read-only BMC identity.
manual_activity: The platform/BMC owner supplies the expected Type 30 manufacturer and connection-mode fields plus redaction/correlation policy; an operator verifies the same-SUT protected path while automation performs the read-only comparison.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS, SMBIOS and BMC identity
Expected Type 30 manufacturer string and inbound/outbound connection-mode bits
Policy for missing, unknown, vendor or legacy capability values
Approved mapping between SMBIOS OOB identity and the physical/logical BMC instance
Endpoint, serial, MAC and credential redaction/access-control policy
Supported dmidecode/parser and protected evidence storage
safety_requirements: Keep the procedure read-only; do not change BMC users, network, certificates, firmware or power state
Do not attempt a remote-control action merely because a capability bit is set
Do not clear logs before relevant baseline evidence is retained
Never put passwords on the command line or disable host-key verification
Capture complete raw output/status under access control and redact only the delivered copy, preserving auditable protected evidence
Bind OS and optional BMC evidence to the same SUT without exposing secrets
Stop on identity mismatch, secret exposure or ambiguous legacy semantics
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, expected Type 30 matrix and redaction rules
Collect complete raw `dmidecode --type 30` through protected access
Parse manufacturer and every inbound/outbound connection flag
Compare exact values and preserve raw-to-parsed mapping
Optionally collect a minimal authenticated read-only BMC identity for same-SUT correlation
Report comparison and no-management-change audit without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve manufacturer/connection-mode expectations and BMC mapping
Define sensitive-field redaction and evidence access
Resolve legacy capability versus current BMC service discrepancies
Review evidence and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Type 30 selector matches the source, but a heading filter hides the manufacturer and connection flags, while sshpass and disabled host-key checking expose secrets and undermine SUT identity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected authenticated OS access to run unfiltered `dmidecode --type 30`, retain complete protected output/status and apply approved redaction to delivered evidence; perform no OOB control action.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Type 30 scope, SPEC comparison, private script and 10/10-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: TYPE30 OOB IDENTITY AND CONNECTION MATRIX REQUIRED
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the raw Type 30 manufacturer and connection-mode bit field, compare it to the approved legacy-capability matrix and separately correlate the exact BMC identity without testing remote actuation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds full bit-level parsing, same-SUT/BMC correlation, sensitive-data controls and a capability-versus-live-service boundary.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A decoder heading cannot prove which connection modes or manufacturer are advertised, and current BMC reachability cannot substitute for the SMBIOS record.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Type 30 may describe a legacy remote-access mechanism and does not attest current BMC network security, authentication strength or service availability.

project_override_considerations: If the platform intentionally omits Type 30, that zero-record expectation must be approved. Redfish/IPMI reachability may be supplemental identity evidence but cannot silently replace the SMBIOS structure or authorize control operations.
expected_evidence: Redacted SUT/BIOS/SMBIOS/BMC identity, timestamp and approved Type 30 matrix
Protected complete raw Type 30 stdout/stderr and exit status
Parsed manufacturer plus inbound/outbound connection flags and raw encodings
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently target SMBIOS Type 30 Out-of-Band Remote Access information. Missing expected fields and BMC identity rules are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The Type 30 collection and comparison are deterministic once the expected capability matrix, BMC mapping and redaction policy are supplied.

review_improvement: Retains the correct Type 30 read while adding connection-bit evidence, exact BMC identity, secret-safe handling and a boundary between advertised capability and live management service.
independent_technical_reasoning: Out-of-band capability metadata and an operational BMC session are not equivalent. Type 30 acceptance is the firmware-advertised manufacturer/connection-bit record for this SUT; proving current remote access would introduce different credentials, network and control risks and cannot be inferred from those bits.
